title: Hall's parents and their attitude to his music
summary: His parents' work and their payment for lessons without any other involvement.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Let's see -- addendum to part one -- we were talking about your early life in Philadelphia and a little bit about your father, but you wanted to bring out who your mother and father were and a little bit about them.
Yes. My mother was Alene K. Hall. It's funny that her middle initial was K, because my nickname has been Al Kay Hall (inaudible), and mine is W. (Laughter.) And my father's Henry.

Henry Hall was a cement finisher. And my mother was a dietician at the University of Pennsylvania. At my age ten a number of doctors bought my first bass, and I came out of high school and learned to play bass fiddle. And she retired from there. My dad was a cement finisher. I just wanted to mention that.
And they encouraged you in music?
Not any more than just to make sure you had the instruments?
You must understand that I was doing something sinful.
Yeah, but let's put it this way.
No. Put it this way. They paid for my lessons and saw that I practiced. But their participation was nil.
